chart.title: Solar photovoltaic module prices vs. cumulative capacity
chart.subtitle: Average price of solar modules versus cumulative installed capacity. Prices are expressed in US dollars per watt, adjusted for inflation. Cumulative solar capacity is measured in megawatts.
chart.note: Costs are expressed in constant 2025 US$ per watt. Global estimates are used before 2010; European market benchmarks thereafter due to limited data availability.

cost.descriptionShort: Average price of solar photovoltaic modules, in US dollars per watt, adjusted for inflation.
cost.descriptionKey:
- Solar photovoltaic module prices refer to the cost of the solar panel itself, and do not include installation or other system components.
- Prices are compiled from four sources: Nemet (2009) for 1975–2003, Farmer & Lafond (2016) for 2004–2009, IRENA's Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024 report for 2010–2019, and IRENA's Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025 report for 2020 onward.
- Due to limited data availability, from 2010 onward we use benchmark prices for modules sold in Europe, which IRENA reports based on data from the trading platform pvXchange. Up to 2019, we use IRENA's module prices, which are based on thin-film modules until late 2013 and on a global price index after that. IRENA has stopped publishing this index, so from 2020 we use its price for mainstream modules, which are standard crystalline silicon modules.
- Historical prices have been adjusted for inflation using the [World Bank's US GDP deflator (linked series)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS.AD?locations=US).
cost.descriptionProcessing:
- Historical photovoltaic cost data between 1975 and 2003 has been taken from Nemet (2009), and between 2004 and 2009 from Farmer & Lafond (2016).
- From 2010 to 2019, prices come from the global module price index in IRENA's Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024 report (the 'Thin film a-Si/u-Si or Global Price Index (from Q4 2013)' series), based on pvXchange benchmarks for modules sold in Europe. IRENA dropped this index from its later reports.
- From 2020 onward, prices come from the 'Mainstream' module series in IRENA's Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2025 report, also based on pvXchange benchmarks for modules sold in Europe. Between 2020 and 2023, the two series differ by less than 20%, so we join them without rescaling either one.
- Prices from Nemet (2009), Farmer & Lafond (2016), and IRENA's global price index have been converted to 2025 US$ using the US GDP deflator (linked series), to account for the effects of inflation. The deflator data is available from the [World Bank World Development Indicators](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS.AD?locations=US).
